cabins.label: Korra's Quarters
cabins.knock: Nothing. The First Officer is on OPS and everybody on this deck knows it.
cabins.inside: A shrine, a shelf of paper books, and a bunk made so tightly it could be inspected.

cabins.label: Dacks' Quarters
cabins.knock: No answer. There is music playing in there, though, and nobody in to hear it.
cabins.inside: Books to the ceiling and a GAYAN lute on a stand, tuned.

cabins.label: Jack's Quarters
cabins.knock: Nothing. He is on the ring. He is always on the ring.
cabins.inside: Six crates of stock he has not mentioned to anybody, and an open ledger.

cabins.label: O'Brain's Quarters
cabins.knock: No answer, and a note on the door in engineering shorthand that means BACK NEVER.
cabins.inside: A workbench, a tool rack, and something half-built he has not named yet.

cabins.label: Bashad's Quarters
cabins.knock: Nothing. The Infirmary never closes and neither, apparently, does he.
cabins.inside: A hydroponic tray under a grow-light, and a medical library nobody else could read.

cabins.label: Warf's Quarters
cabins.knock: Three seconds of nothing, and then: "IT IS OPEN." It was not open.
cabins.inside: A punchbag, a rack of things with edges, and a bunk with no blanket on it.

cabins.label: Vor's Quarters
cabins.knock: No answer. She keeps a pitch on the ring and she keeps it long hours.
cabins.inside: Stock she has not put out yet, and a tray of something she is growing herself.

cabins.label: The Pells' Quarters
cabins.knock: A woman’s voice, unhurried: "It is open, if you can get the door to agree."
cabins.inside: A cot beside the bunk, a line of washing across the corner, and a board game left out.

cabins.label: Seth's Quarters
cabins.knock: Nothing, but there is a candle burning in there, which is against about four regulations.
cabins.inside: A shrine with the candles lit, washing on a line, and a tray of herbs.

cabins.label: Grell's Quarters
cabins.knock: No answer. GRELL walks the ring all day and does not say why.
cabins.inside: A bench covered in salvage, sorted by something that is not size or value.

cabins.label: Nag's Quarters
cabins.knock: Nothing, and a small sign: PREMISES ALARMED. It is not alarmed.
cabins.inside: Shelves of stock with the prices showing, and a strongbox under the bunk.

cabins.label: Pav's Quarters
cabins.knock: "Come in, STEWARD. It is not locked." It is locked. He has forgotten again.
cabins.inside: A shrine, a games board, and eighty years of paper.

clerics.name: KEEPER OPA
clerics.title: Keeper of the Shrine
clerics.greeting: THE EIGHT keep no office hours, STEWARD. Neither do I.
clerics.bio: Keeps the shrine on the only one of MIGHT'S twelve that was given a temple. She lit the first flame the day the yards went quiet, and it has not been out since.

lines.text: KEEPER.
STEWARD. You walk past this door a great deal and through it very rarely.
The flame does not mind. I mention it only for the record.

guests.name: QUIRK
guests.title: Proprietor
guests.bio: Owns the bar, the daba wheel and the holosuites. Owns a piece of most other things too.

lines.text: QUIRK.
STEWARD! Sit, sit. First one is on the house. The second is where I make it back.
It is not, of course. But it sounds better than the alternative.

replies.text: Everything. Synthale, spring wine, something blue that I am legally required not to name.
The wheel is warm and the holosuites are booked out until second shift. Sadly.
Always. Whether you can afford it is a separate conversation.
A freighter came in light and left heavy. Make of that what you like, STEWARD.
My nephew? He is polishing glasses when he should be counting them.
He has been running about the ring with YOUR boy all week. Whatever they are up to, I had no part in it.
...I would like that on the record.
Bring latinum next time. And an appetite.

guests.name: NAG
guests.title: Quirk's nephew
guests.bio: Wants a commission more than he wants the bar. Has not told his uncle that yet.

lines.text: NAG.
STEWARD! Sir. Steward sir.
JACK said you would not mind. About the thing. Which there is no thing about.

replies.text: The NOTHING thing. The absolutely-nothing-in-cargo-bay-four thing.
...ask JACK. He is on the ring. He is better at this than me.
I want a uniform. I want to stand on OPS and say things like "aye, Captain".
Uncle QUIRK says the only uniform worth wearing is an apron with a full till behind it.
I say a KUFAN can do both.
Aye! ...sir. Aye sir. I have been practising.

guests.name: CAPT. BENNY
guests.title: Commanding Officer, SPACE STATION 8
guests.bio: Runs the station, the ring, the docking clamps and, on the days it comes up, the Temple. Reports to the STEWARD, which he does on time and at length. Would rather be running a ship.

lines.text: CAPTAIN.
STEWARD. Come in — and shut it behind you. Everything on this station is a corridor and the whole ring can hear.
My report is filed. It is also four days late, and you have not mentioned it, which I am choosing to enjoy.

replies.text: Standing. Which for one of KING MIGHT'S own yards is the least she should do, and rather more than the last two I served on.
She is the EIGHTH. Twelve of them went up: one over every planet, one shadowing the MACHINE FLEET, and the one west of yours that nobody has answered a hail from in years.
O'BRAIN tells me the same thing every morning in more words and with more swearing.
You have been watching QUIRK’S screen. So has everyone else, which is the problem.
The SIXTH GATE held for six hours. Command says there is no cause for alarm and Command is four sectors away.
I want the pylons crewed and I want nobody saying the word evacuation on my ring. Both. In that order.
MIGHT did. Or his yards did, which on the paperwork is the same signature.
Eight is the middle of the twelve and the only one with a Temple, and the KEEPERS will tell you those two facts are related. The engineers will tell you it is where the ore ran out.
Both of them are standing in a ring the old King cut out of one piece. I have stopped arguing with either.

topics.label: Your son is on the ring.

replies.text: JACK. Yes. With QUIRK’S nephew, doing something in a cargo bay nobody logged.
I know. I have known for a week. I have been waiting to see whether he tells me.
...he is fourteen and he is running a business. I am not as angry as I am supposed to be.
KEEPER OPA keeps the flame and I keep out of it, and we have both been very careful about that for three years.
Go and stand at the shrine some time. I am not telling you what to believe. I am telling you it is quiet in there.
Plasma injectors, a second Constable, and eight uninterrupted hours.
Take the first one to the Chief. The other two are not in anybody’s gift.
STEWARD. I will have the pylon roster on your desk before you are back down the lift.

guests.name: DR. BASHAD
guests.title: Chief Medical Officer
guests.bio: Brilliant, and quite happy for you to know it. Has never once lost a patient he was allowed to reach in time.

lines.text: DOCTOR.
STEWARD. Sit on the bed, not the console. The console bills you.

replies.text: Hold still. This will sting for exactly as long as it takes you to complain about it.
There. Try to bring the same number of limbs back next time.
Three in overnight. A conduit burn from ENGINEERING, a bar-related jaw, and a GAYAN pilgrim with a bad cough.
The cough worries me more than the other two put together.
Yes. You are running on four hours of sleep and a UR black, STEWARD.
I cannot order you to rest. I can write it down repeatedly until someone notices.
Any time. Preferably a time when you are not bleeding.

guests.name: ODD the O
guests.title: Co-Head of Security
guests.bio: Not from anywhere anyone has been. Holds a shape the way the rest of us hold a grudge.

lines.text: CONSTABLE.
STEWARD. Before you ask: yes, I know. I knew before it happened.

replies.text: Four hundred and six people came aboard this week. I have opinions about nine of them.
Two of the nine drink at QUIRK'S. That is not a coincidence, it is a business model.
WARF believes security is a wall. I believe it is a question.
Between the two of us the station is quite thoroughly covered.

topics.label: Have you seen JACK and NAG?

replies.text: Cargo bay four. Twice. They think the corridor camera is the only one.
I have not filed it. Yet. A word with the CAPTAIN about his boy and I will not have to.
I always do.

guests.name: WARF
guests.title: Co-Head of Security
guests.bio: Fought his way onto this station and has been standing very still in it ever since. It does not suit him. He is superb at it.

lines.text: LIEUTENANT.
STEWARD. The docking ring is secure. The Promenade is secure.
QUIRK is not secure, but he is CONTAINED.

replies.text: Two ships at the upper pylons, both cleared. One at the lower, still arguing about it.
I have posted a guard. The argument has become much shorter.
It would be an HONOUR, STEWARD.
I will go easy on you. ...I will consider going easy on you.
The Constable is thorough. He is also EVERYWHERE, which I find difficult to plan around.
He says the same of me. We have agreed to be a problem for other people instead.
Sir.

guests.name: O'BRAIN
guests.title: Chief of Operations
guests.bio: Keeps a station built by somebody else, out of parts made by somebody else again, running on a schedule set by you.

lines.text: CHIEF.
STEWARD. Do not lean on that. Or that. Honestly, just stand in the middle.

replies.text: The core is at ninety-one percent and I would very much like to know why it is not ninety-four.
Give me eight hours and a shift that does not get called away and it will be.
Deck six environmental, a turbolift that only stops where it feels like it, and the replicator in QUIRK'S.
I fixed the replicator first. I am not proud of the reasoning.
Plasma injectors. Six of them. And for people to stop opening panels they cannot close.
The CAPTAIN'S boy and the KUFAN lad have been in cargo bay four twice this week, STEWARD. Just so you have heard it from me as well as from him.
Always am.

guests.name: KORRA
guests.title: First Officer
guests.bio: Fought a long war, and then a longer paper one to get this station signed over to GAYA. Now runs its duty roster, and takes that every bit as seriously.

lines.text: COMMANDER.
STEWARD. OPS is yours whenever you want it. I have kept it warm and mostly upright.

replies.text: All decks report. Docking ring at two thirds. Provisional government wants a report by end of shift.
I have written most of it. You will want to change the ending. You always do.
The KEEPER asked after you. She noticed you have not been down.
I did not make excuses for you, STEWARD. That is not my department.
I spent eight years getting this station signed over. Now I have it and it needs a plumber.
...I would not trade it. Do not put that in the log.
Aye, STEWARD.

guests.name: DACKS
guests.title: Chief Science Officer
guests.bio: Older than the station, the sector and most of the paperwork. Carries several lifetimes and all of their bad habits.

lines.text: LIEUTENANT.
STEWARD. Or your father's name, which I still reach for first.
Three hundred years and I cannot decide which of you I am talking to.

replies.text: Opening on a schedule nobody set, which is my favourite kind of schedule.
The neutrino count is up eleven percent. That is either a passage or a very good imitation of one.
A previous host of mine sat in a chair very like yours and got the same look you are giving me now.
He was wrong, as it happens. But he was wrong with style, and the crew followed him anyway.
I will take your latinum and three of your officers' as well.
It is not cheating if you have had six lifetimes to practise.
Bring the good UR black.

guests.name: GAROK
guests.title: Tailor. Plain and simple.
guests.bio: The only one of his people left on the station. Sews beautifully. Answers questions beautifully too, and rather less honestly.

lines.text: GAROK.
STEWARD! What a genuine pleasure. And so unexpected, at precisely the hour you always come.

replies.text: Of course you do. Shoulders like that, in a jacket like THAT.
Stand on the block. Do not talk. It ruins the line of the neck.
I am a tailor, STEWARD. Plain. Simple.
It is a marvellous story. I have told it so many times that I have begun to enjoy it myself.
Everything. Nobody watches what they say in front of the man taking their measurements.
A freighter came in light and left heavy, for example. But QUIRK will have told you that, and charged you for it.
Do come back. The hem will not fit itself, and I will not stop hoping.

guests.name: JACK
guests.title: The Captain's son
guests.bio: The CAPTAIN'S boy. Fourteen, and running a station-wide enterprise out of a cargo bay with a KUFAN for a business partner.

lines.text: JACK.
STEWARD. Sir. I did not see you. Which is usually the idea.

guests.name: ENS. TARR
guests.title: Off watch
guests.bio: Came off gamma four hours ago and has not managed to leave the wardroom since.

lines.text: Ensign.
Sir. Off duty, sir — I can put the boots back on if you—
...no. Right. Off duty. I will sit back down.

replies.text: Quiet. Too quiet, some watches. You can hear the ring turning through the deck plates.
You stop noticing it after a month. Then one night you notice it again.
The Captain’s boy is up and down this corridor at all hours.
Carrying things. Never the same thing twice.
Not my business, sir. I only mention it because you asked.
Aye sir. In a minute, sir.

loot.name: a cold cup of UR black

guests.name: CREWMAN BEK
guests.title: Environmental systems
guests.bio: Third time this month on this corridor. It is always the same junction and it is never the same fault.

lines.text: Trouble?
Air handler, STEWARD. Twelve is running warm and eight is running cold and they share a duct.
MIGHT'S plumbing. Built by people who were paid by the metre and knew it.

replies.text: I can fix it. I have fixed it. It will want fixing again on Thursday.
CHIEF O’BRAIN says the same. He says it in more words.
DR. BASHAD, sir, and he is polite about it, which is worse.
LT. WARF has never complained once. I do not think LT. WARF feels temperature.
STEWARD.

guests.name: OLD PAV
guests.title: Twelve-B, and has been a while
guests.bio: Was here the day MIGHT'S yards went quiet and was here the morning after. Has not felt any need to go anywhere since.

lines.text: Good evening.
It is. They mostly are now. That is the part nobody says out loud.

topics.label: How long have you been aboard?

replies.text: Longer than the sign over the bar, and that sign has been up a while.
I had this same cabin when it had a different number on it. And a different door.
Full. Which is the best thing you can say about a corridor.
The PELLS’ girl chalks a game on my floor and I chase her off it. That is our arrangement.
NAG? He weighed my post. My POST, STEWARD.
Then he carried it in for me, and would not take anything for it.
He will be all right, that one. Do not tell him I said so.
I DO lock it. Then I forget I locked it and stand out here arguing with it.
Take the code. Two-two-one-nine. If you find me shut out, let me in.
And if you want a cup of something while you are in there, the pot is on the shelf.
Goodnight, STEWARD. Mind the chalk.

guests.name: MEELA PELL
guests.title: Four-B, and nine
guests.bio: Owns the chalk, the game, and by extension this stretch of deck.

lines.text: Hello.
You are the one off OPS.
You have to go round. The squares are wet. They are not but you have to go round.

replies.text: JACK did. He is rubbish at it now because his legs got long.
He gave me a box of tea once and mum made him take it back.
He minds LOUDLY.
Then he stands there and watches to see if I get to eight.

topics.label: How do you get back in at teatime?

replies.text: Four-four-four-four. Mum says it is a terrible one.
Dad says nobody would ever guess it because it is too stupid.
...I was not supposed to say it out loud, was I.
You still have to go round.

guests.name: TESSA VOR
guests.title: Kiosk trader
guests.bio: Sells honeyroot, firewrap and whatever the last freighter could not shift. Has held the same pitch since the yards went quiet.

lines.text: Anything worth buying?
Honeyroot sticks, STEWARD, and a crate of JIDDA tea that has seen better decades.
You want the tea. Everyone says they do not, and then they do.

guests.name: ENS. PELL
guests.title: Ensign, gamma shift
guests.bio: Three weeks aboard. Still walks the whole ring the long way round because she has not worked out which way is shorter.

lines.text: Ensign.
STEWARD! Sir. Ma— STEWARD.
Gamma shift, sir. All quiet. Except at QUIRK'S, which I understand is normal.

guests.name: A PILGRIM
guests.title: Come for the temple
guests.bio: Came up on the morning transport with nothing but a coat and a reason.

lines.text: Welcome aboard.
I waited a long time to be allowed to stand here, STEWARD.
Point me at the temple and I will not trouble you further.

guests.name: BREL
guests.title: Off the freight line
guests.bio: Works the lower pylon. Comes in at the end of a shift, has exactly two, and goes home.

lines.text: Evening.
STEWARD. Sit down or do not, but do not HOVER, you are worse than QUIRK.
...that was rude. It has been a shift. Sit down.

replies.text: Eleven hours on a loading arm that keeps asking me if I am sure.
I am sure. I have been sure for eleven hours.
Whatever he pours you FIRST. The second one he has had time to think about.
I intend to. Both of them.

guests.name: SANNA VOSK
guests.title: Off duty, and saying so
guests.bio: Runs the night board in Ops. Drinks here because it is the one room on the station nobody pages her in.

lines.text: Ensign.
Off DUTY, STEWARD. I am a civilian for another forty minutes.
You may address me as SANNA, or as nothing at all. Either is fine.

replies.text: On the board? Three ships, none of them arguing. That is a quiet night.
In here? QUIRK has lost twice at his own wheel and taken it very personally.
The lower pylon clamp reads two degrees warm and has for a week.
I have logged it four times. Tell the CHIEF I said hello.
Thirty-eight minutes. Do not hurry me.

guests.name: TEEK
guests.title: Waiting on somebody
guests.bio: Has been at that table since the first bell with one drink and both eyes on the door.

lines.text: Expecting someone?
She said the second bell. It has been the second bell for some time.
I am not WORRIED. I am seated. There is a difference.

replies.text: Her name is not the STEWARD'S business, with respect.
...if a tall one in a grey coat asks, tell her the table by the wheel.
She will. She is never early and she has never once not come.
Thank you. That was kinder than it needed to be.

topics.label: I will leave you to it.

replies.text: Please.

guests.name: MARN
guests.title: Owes the wheel money
guests.bio: Has a system. The system has cost him four hundred credits and he is refining it.

lines.text: Any luck?
LUCK is for people without a SYSTEM, STEWARD.
...the system is currently down four hundred. It is a LONG system.

replies.text: You watch the outer ring. You count. When it has been cold a while, you go.
It has been cold a while for six weeks.
That is what my sister says. She says it in a LETTER, from a long way away.
So I have some time yet.
SYSTEM.

guests.name: ROSK
guests.title: Guest of the Constable
guests.bio: Picked up on the upper pylon with a manifest that did not match the crates under it. Says the crates are a misunderstanding. Says it very well.

lines.text: Comfortable?
STEWARD! A friendly face. Come to let me out, have you.
No. No, you have the LOOK of a man who is going to ask me questions instead.

replies.text: NOTHING that was not on the manifest. The manifest was simply... abbreviated.
It is a long form, STEWARD. Nobody fills in all of it.
The CONSTABLE has been standing THERE for two days looking at me.
I have offered him money, a story and a game of cards. He took the story.

topics.label: How long are you in for?

replies.text: Until somebody up the pylon remembers whose name is on the lease.
I am in no hurry. The bunk is better than my own.
I have very little choice, but thank you.

guests.name: DEPUTY RYNN
guests.title: GAYAN deputy
guests.bio: Walks the ring twice a shift and has done since before there was a ring worth walking.

lines.text: Deputy.
STEWARD. Two laps down, four to go.
The Constable says a walked corridor is a quiet corridor. He is not wrong. He is rarely wrong. It is exhausting.

guests.name: CREWMAN BODE
guests.title: Off duty, briefly
guests.bio: Has forty minutes and a list of three things, and will manage one of them.

lines.text: Crewman.
STEWARD! I am off duty, sir. Very off duty.
I am going to the Replimat and then I am going to sit down. That is the whole plan.

guests.name: CAPT. MOSS
guests.title: Freighter master
guests.bio: Runs ore out to the belt and back. Docked at upper pylon two and in no hurry to leave.

lines.text: Captain Moss.
STEWARD. Your docking clamps are the best in the sector and your customs officer is the worst.
I mean that as a compliment to one of them.

guests.name: PRYLAR SETH
guests.title: Of the order
guests.bio: Walks the ring in the slow lane, and has never once been in anyone's way.

lines.text: Prylar.
STEWARD. The KEEPER keeps the flame; I keep the walk.
It is the same job at a different speed.

guests.name: MIRA
guests.title: Daba girl, on her break
guests.bio: Twenty minutes of not being shouted at by anybody, and she intends to spend all of them walking.

lines.text: Mira.
STEWARD. Do not tell QUIRK you saw me out here.
I get twenty minutes. He counts them. He counts EVERYTHING.

guests.name: GRELL
guests.title: Passing through
guests.bio: Three days aboard, no cargo declared, and an opinion about every price on the ring.

lines.text: And you are?
Nobody! A visitor. An admirer of your beautiful, beautiful docking fees.
Which are too high. Since you ask. Which you did not.

guests.name: TECH VOSS
guests.title: One of O'Brain's
guests.bio: Carrying a part to somewhere else. Always carrying a part to somewhere else.

lines.text: Tech.
STEWARD — sorry — plasma coupling — deck four — cannot stop —
...tell the Chief I did not stop!

guests.name: HANNA VELS
guests.title: Lives on deck seven
guests.bio: Moved aboard the month GAYA was handed the keys and has not seen a reason to move off.

lines.text: Evening.
Evening, STEWARD. My boy asked me today whether the station was always ours.
I did not have a short answer for him. I am still working on one.

guests.name: TORVIN
guests.title: Her boy
guests.bio: Nine. Wants to know how big the GATE is, in units of this station.

lines.text: Hello.
Are you the STEWARD? The one the CAPTAIN has to write to?
JACK says you are. JACK says a lot of things.

guests.name: SISTER ANU
guests.title: Meets the transports
guests.bio: Waits at the airlock for every arrival and walks them round the ring once, whether they asked or not.

lines.text: Sister.
STEWARD. Four pilgrims off the morning transport and not one of them could find the temple.
It is the only door on the ring with a flame behind it. I do not know how they manage it.

guests.name: OLD PAV
guests.title: Honeyroot, hot
guests.bio: Has the stall at bearing two-two-five and walks the ring when trade is slow, which is most of it.

lines.text: Pav.
STEWARD. Honeyroot? On the house. It is always on the house and you never take it.
One of these days you will take it and I will have to think of a new joke.

guests.name: CONST. DEP. KAL
guests.title: Outer lane patrol
guests.bio: Walks the outer lane so the Deputy can walk the inner one. Between them nothing crosses the ring unseen.

lines.text: Anything?
Nothing, STEWARD. Which the Constable says is the most suspicious thing of all.
I have stopped asking him what he means.

guests.name: ENS. TALB
guests.title: One of Bashad's
guests.bio: Runs the infirmary errands, and has learned which way round the ring is quicker at which hour.

lines.text: Ensign.
STEWARD. Two hyposprays and a very slow turbolift, sir.
I have started walking. It is faster and the Doctor pretends not to notice.

guests.name: MOL
guests.title: Upper pylon three
guests.bio: Loads and unloads whatever comes in, and can tell you the mass of a crate by looking at it.

lines.text: Long shift?
Every shift, STEWARD.
Ore in, ore out, and QUIRK charges me for the walk between them.

guests.name: SUB-WARDEN KASPAR
guests.title: Kufa Station, Operations
guests.bio: Twelve years on the plot table. Has never once been down to the world she has spent her whole career looking at.

lines.text: Sub-Warden.
PILOT. You are docked, you are logged, and nothing you are carrying is my problem yet.
Keep it that way and we will get on.

replies.text: Copper. Everything you can see was drawn or rolled downstairs and came up here to be sold somewhere else.
Half the wiring in the nine started on that world. The other half is lying about it.
The black fleet took a station two systems over and put it back in pieces.
We are told that is not a pattern. I plot what I am given, PILOT.
The world's. Not the station's, whatever the plate on my door says.
KADE has been up here twice. Once to open it and once to be photographed opening it.
Do.

guests.name: CREWMAN NIX
guests.title: On the boards
guests.bio: Nebo-born, Kufa-paid, and reminded of the second thing daily.

lines.text: Busy?
The board is quiet. The SUB-WARDEN is not. Those are different weathers, PILOT.

guests.name: KANE
guests.title: Signs hands on
guests.bio: Was a hand himself for nineteen years and has the shoulders to prove it. Will not put a name on your ship he would not sail with.

lines.text: I am looking for crew.
Everybody is. Bench is behind you — look at them before you look at me.
I will tell you what they cost. They will tell you what they are.

replies.text: BRIN can hold a line in weather. TOLL can hold a line in weather and a grudge for ever.
The quiet one at the end has not told me her name and has not needed to.
A share, or a wage, and the wage is cheaper right up until it is not.
Nobody good takes a wage from a stranger, PILOT.
Bench does not go anywhere. Neither do I.

guests.name: BRIN
guests.title: Deck hand, nine years
guests.bio: Off a copper hauler that does not run any more. Waiting rather than begging, and clear on the difference.

lines.text: Waiting long?
Six days. I am not in a hurry and I am not cheap.

guests.name: TOLL
guests.title: Gunner, and says so first
guests.bio: Has been let go by three ships and has three explanations ready.

lines.text: What do you do?
Guns. Before you ask — it was not my fault on any of them.

guests.name: A QUIET ONE
guests.title: Has not said
guests.bio: Sat down on the first morning, has not moved, and KANE has stopped asking.

lines.text: And you are?
Ask KANE what I am worth. Do not ask me what I am.

guests.name: FACTOR KIA
guests.title: Contracts and manifests
guests.bio: Reads a manifest the way other people read a face. Has never lost a crate and will tell you so within a minute of meeting you.

lines.text: What is on the board?
Copper out, PILOT. Copper is always out. The question is where to.
The dock will buy a crate off you at what today is worth. I will pay you for putting it where it is NEEDED. Those are not the same number.

replies.text: ZION wants wire and cannot smelt in that damp. Long run, good money, and the black fleet has been seen on that lane twice this month.
That is why it is good money.
Grain off GAYA, ink off NEBO, and a standing order of incense that is none of my business and goes through anyway.
The board does not improve for being looked at, PILOT.

guests.name: OLD MERRIT
guests.title: Sells what he has heard
guests.bio: Flew for forty years and kept a note of every odd thing he passed. The notes are the business now.

lines.text: What have you got?
Three things, PILOT, and I only ever have three.
One on the world below. One out in the dark. And one somewhere on this station, which is the one people laugh at and the one that is true.

replies.text: There is a cut in the terraces that was worked before the gates and abandoned in a hurry. Things get left when people leave in a hurry.
A hull, cold, off the lane. Nobody logged it going out and nobody has logged it since.
It will still be there. That is the thing about the dark.
Aye. Laugh.
This ring was built in four pieces and joined in orbit, and one of the joins has a space behind it that is on nobody's plan but mine.
It keeps. Most of it has kept four hundred years.

guests.name: ASSAYER VETCH
guests.title: Buys old things
guests.bio: Can date a gate-shard by the seam in it. Pays fairly and enjoys explaining exactly how fairly.

lines.text: You buy relics.
I buy SOME relics, PILOT. Anyone will buy any of them; that is a scrapyard.
Put it on the glass and we will find out which of us is having a good day.

replies.text: Gate-work. Shard glass, sigil stone, anything with the eight notches on it.
And I will pay over the odds for a thing with NINE, if you ever find one. Nobody ever has.
One piece, under its worth, to a face I have not seen before. Once.
After that you pay what everybody pays, and you will find I am still the cheapest in the nine.
It is four centuries old. It will wait an afternoon.

guests.name: SISTER HOLLY
guests.title: Keeps the garden
guests.bio: Came up with a seed case and a six-month contract eleven years ago. The contract ran out. The garden did not.

lines.text: This is not what I expected in the middle of a copper station.
No. That is rather the point of it, PILOT.
They gave me the middle because nothing else would fit there. Now every soul aboard walks through my beds four times a shift.

topics.label: How does anything grow up here?

replies.text: Copper frame, glass roof, water on a loop, and a great deal of arguing with OPERATIONS about the lamps.
The trick is not the growing. The trick is the eleven years.
All of them. The FACTOR eats her lunch on that bench and tells it things she would not tell KANE.
If you want to know what is happening on this station, PILOT, do not ask at a counter. Sit down.
It is the only room. The rest is corridor with a job in it.

guests.name: DOCKER PELL
guests.title: Half an hour left
guests.bio: Eats here every shift because it is the only place on the station that smells of anything.

lines.text: Good spot.
Best on the ring. Do not tell the SUB-WARDEN or there will be a rota for it.

guests.name: A GAYAN TRAVELLER
guests.title: Waiting on a berth
guests.bio: Three days off a grain hauler and two days short of the next one.

lines.text: Travelling?
Trying to. There is one ship a week to GAYA and I have watched it leave twice.
At least there is somewhere to sit and be annoyed about it.

guests.name: A SMALL KUFAN
guests.title: Should be at lessons
guests.bio: Has worked out that nobody crossing the garden in a hurry ever looks down.

lines.text: Should you be here?
There are FISH.
...there are not fish. But there could be, and I am waiting.
